1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

1: # OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions
2: 
3: Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
4: Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.
5: 
6: ## Wiki index
7: 
8: - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
9: - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
10: - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
11: - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
12: - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
13: - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)
14: 
15: 
16: ## Main project file
17: 
18: The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).
19: 
20: Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
21: aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
22: initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
23: default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
24: the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
25: Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
26: for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
27: helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
28: Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
29: project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
30: dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.
31: 
32: ## Shell timing
33: 
34: When writing shell scripts,
35: always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
36: Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
37: the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
38: slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
39: interactive shell commands.
40: 
41: ## Ideas
42: 
43: Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
44: `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
45: `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.
46: 
47: 
48: 
49: 
50: ## Links in handoffs
51: 
52: When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
53: link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
54: requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
55: than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
56: the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.
57: 
58: When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.
59: 
60: ## OpenCode GitHub Actions
61: 
62: To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
63: Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
64: The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
65: verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.
66: 
67: When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
68: Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
69: logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
70: for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
71: which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.
72: 
73: Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
74: Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
75: Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
76: Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
77: Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.
78: 
79: Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
80: Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.
81: 
82: To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
83: `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
84: then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
85: with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.
86: 
87: When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
88: over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
89: same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
90: is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
91: live log evidence can be collected.
92: 
93: For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:
94: 
95: ```sh
96: bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
97: ```
98: 
99: The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
100: request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
101: `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
102: inspecting the runner.
103: 
104: ## Mac SSH access
105: 
106: The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
107: stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
108: commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:
109: 
110: ```sh
111: ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
112: ```
113: 
114: The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.
115: 
116: ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker
117: 
118: Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
119: or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:
120: 
121: ```sh
122: bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
123: ```
124: 
125: For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
126: use the same key:
127: 
128: ```sh
129: ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
130:   -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
131:   -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
132:   -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
133: ```
134: 
135: Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
136: can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
137: worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
138: print secrets while inspecting a worker.
